walkthrough:
Group the terms to factorise the four-term trigonometric expression:
$$3\cos\theta(2\tan\theta - 1) + 2(2\tan\theta - 1) = 0$$

Solve the first factor on the interval $0^\circ \le \theta \le 180^\circ$:
$$2\tan\theta - 1 = 0 \implies \tan\theta = \frac{1}{2} \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.5) \approx 26.6^\circ$$

Solve the second factor on the interval $0^\circ \le \theta \le 180^\circ$:
$$3\cos\theta + 2 = 0 \implies \cos\theta = -\frac{2}{3} \implies \theta = 180^\circ - \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \approx 180^\circ - 48.19^\circ = 131.8^\circ$$
